article_content: Samantha Azzopardi, a 25-year-old Australian woman, was found in Ireland and initially suspected to be a victim of human trafficking due to her age being misjudged. However, it was later revealed that she had apparent health problems and a complex background, including having around 40 aliases. Azzopardi was repatriated to Australia after being in the care of health authorities in Dublin.

Pada mulanya, terdapatlah kebimbangan bahawa dia adalah mangsa manusia lalu lintas, namun tetapi kemudian didapati bahawa dia mempunyai masalah kesihatan dan mempunyai latar belakang. Azzopardi, yang mempunyai kira-kira 40 nama samaran, telah berada dalam jagaan pihak di Dublin sebelum dipulangkan semula ke Australia.

article_content: A teacher's aide in Iowa has been suspended after an anonymous caller revealed her involvement in a decades-old crime. Paula Pace, 64, has been working at the school since 1998, but her past has caught up with her. An anonymous caller contacted the school, revealing that Pace was once known as Paula Baniszewski, who was jailed for her role in the torture and killing of 16-year-old Sylvia Likens in 1965. The incident occurred when Likens and her sister moved in with the Baniszewski family in Indiana for the summer. The Baniszewskis, including Paula, subjected the girls to physical and emotional abuse, which ultimately led to Likens' death. The school district has suspended Pace pending an investigation.

Paula Pace, 64, telah bekerja di sekolah sejak 1998, tetapi masa lalunya telah menangkapnya. Seorang penggil misterius menelefon sekolah, mendedahkan bahawa Pace dulunya Paula Baniszewski, yang pernah dijebloskan atas perannya dalam penyiksaan dan pembunuhan terhadap seorang gadis berusia 16 tahun, Sylvia Likens, pada tahun 1965. Insiden itu terjadi ketika Likens dan adiknya pindah ke rumah keluarga Baniszewski di Indiana untuk musim panas. Keluarga Baniszewski, termasuk Paula, mengani gadis-gadis itu dengan kekerasan fizikal dan emosional, yang akhirnya menyebabkan kematian Likens.
